Strategy Lab — trading plans & research

How to read this
  • Backtest window: daily bars 2005→now (~21 yrs where available). Each ticker is split by time: the first 70% is in-sample (IS) — used to pick the strategy — and the last 30% is out-of-sample (OOS) — a holdout used to judge it on data it never saw.
  • Sharpe ratio: return per unit of risk. >1 is strong, 0.5–1 decent, <0 is losing on a risk-adjusted basis. We choose on IS Sharpe but show OOS numbers, so the headline figures are honest.
  • Walk-forward: the plan is re-tested on several separate time slices; the % shown is how many were profitable. High = consistent, not a one-off fluke.
  • Verdict: ★ High confidence = recommended and passed the robustness stress-test (PSR>90%, profit-probability>75%, low fragility). ✓ Recommended = held up OOS and beat buy&hold and walk-forward ≥75%. Held OOS = profitable OOS but weaker. Marginal = didn't clear the bar.
  • PSR & Monte Carlo (click a row): PSR = probability the edge is real given the track record (near 1.0 = strong, 0.5 = coin-flip). Monte Carlo reshuffles the plan's trades thousands of times to show a range of returns and the drawdown in a bad ordering — and flags plans with a high chance of a >30% drawdown as fragile.
  • WFO+ (walk-forward): the strictest test — re-pick the best strategy on each window and trade the next unseen one (how the weekly rescan actually works). Green = consistently profitable forward. Reality check: most plans stay profitable but don't beat buy&hold on strongly-trending stocks, because a long-only timing strategy sits out part of the run. Read these as risk-managed, selective participation (lower drawdown, defined stops) — not a promise of beating the index. Timing adds the most value on range-bound / mean-reverting names.
  • Exit/stop is the risk rule (e.g. sl_15 = 15% stop, trail_10 = 10% trailing, atr_2x = 2×ATR stop, sl10_tp20 = 10% stop / 20% target). Click any plan row for full detail.
